issues.description: The problem statement contains two conflicting signatures for the milk-related method. The UML and example code use messageOnMilk() with no parameters (returning a String), but the textual specification in Part 2 describes messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and prescribes a return format including the volume. The template's commented Main and the solution's Milkable interface and implementations all expect messageOnMilk() without parameters. This conflict will confuse students which signature to implement and may lead to compile errors or test failures if they implement the variant with a double parameter while the template/tests expect the no-argument version.
issues.suggested_fix:
Resolve the conflicting specification. Either:
1) Prefer the no-argument design (recommended to match UML, template Main, and provided solution): Change the Part 2 textual description to require messageOnMilk() returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (remove the double parameter and volume). Update the example return format in Part 2 accordingly.
Or
2) If the intent is to require a milkVolume parameter, update the UML, the template Main usage, the Milkable interface, and all solution implementations to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and adjust calls and return strings to include the volume (e.g. "Seal Clarabelle is milked (volume: 1.5L)").
Choose one consistent signature and update all artifacts (problem text, UML, template code, and tests) to match.

issues.description: Mismatch in the milk-related method signature and expected return format between the problem text and the code artifacts. The problem text (Part 2) specifies messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and instructs that the returned string must include the milk volume ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)"), while the UML earlier in the problem and both template usage and the solution define/use messageOnMilk() with no parameter and a return value that does not include any volume. This creates a direct mapping/confusion for students: they may implement a messageOnMilk method with a double parameter (as the textual requirement states) but the provided template, Main usage, and the solution expect a parameterless method, which leads to compilation/test mismatches and unclear expectations about the required API and return format.
issues.suggested_fix:
Make the requirement and the code agree. Two viable fixes (pick one):

1) Align problem text with the UML/template/solution: change the textual requirement in Part 2 to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and specify the return string as "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". This matches the UML (messageOnMilk(): String), the template Main usage (m.messageOnMilk()), and the current solution implementations.

2) If the intent is to track volume, update the code artifacts to accept a double parameter: change the Milkable interface to String messageOnMilk(double milkVolume); update Goat and Seal to implement the new signature and return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked (volume: [milkVolume]L)"; and update all call sites (e.g., Main and any tests) to pass a milkVolume value. Ensure the UML in the problem statement is also updated to reflect the parameter.

Either fix will remove the conflicting API expectation; prefer option (1) if minimal changes are desired and to match the existing template/solution, or option (2) if the volume requirement is pedagogically important.
